model.description: The A1 DEFAULT actions Scenario and Edit — the two the universalActionBar composes on ALL usages — must ALWAYS open in a NEW TAB, never navigate the current one, from EVERY surface the bar appears on (trace / model / room / task detail / drawer). Losing his place on a phone is the actual pain.

discoverySource.note: A1 default Scenario/Edit must open new-tab always; current-tab context preservation on mobile.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The A1 'Scenario' default action opens the scenario in a NEW TAB.
The A1 'Edit' default action opens the editor in a NEW TAB.

★ 'ALWAYS' = from EVERY surface the universalActionBar is composed on (trace / model / room / task detail / drawer), not just the one currently in view. The word 'always' is part of the requirement — a per-surface exception is a defect.
The CURRENT tab is NOT navigated away — the user keeps his place (losing context on a phone is the actual pain being fixed).
The OTHER actions' behaviour is unchanged (no reverse regression).

★ Device-gated @390 real-WebKit asserting a NEW TAB/WINDOW actually OPENED — assert the RESULT (a new browsing context exists), NOT that a target/attribute is present. A rendered target that never opens is the empty-container class.

★ IMPLEMENTATION HAZARD (by-construction): the new-tab open MUST be triggered SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the tap/user-gesture handler — NO await / fetch / resolve / async ref lookup before window.open. iOS Safari BLOCKS a non-synchronous window.open as a popup: the tab silently never appears, and that failure is INVISIBLE headless. Resolve any URL/ref data BEFORE the tap or open synchronously and navigate the new context after.
